notes.title: 2026 Question Set 17: Give Geographical Reasons
notes.content:
(17) Population is an important resource.                   (July ’19)

Ans. (1) The economic and social growth and development of any country depends upon its quantity and quality of population.

(2) If a country has excess of population or if it has less population than requirement, it results in slow economic growth and development of country.

(3) If a country has optimum and quality population, its economic growth and development speeds up. In this way, population is an important resource.

(18) India’s density of population is high.

Ans. (1) India occupies nearly 2.41 per cent of the world’s total land.

(2) It has nearly 17.58 per cent of the world’s total population.

(3) Thus, India has comparatively less per cent of the world’s total land and more per cent of the world’s total population. Therefore, India’s density of population is high.

(19) Brazil’s population density is very less.

Ans. (1) Brazil occupies nearly 5.6 per cent of the world’s total land.

(2) It has nearly 2.78 per cent of the world’s total population.

(3) Thus, Brazil has comparatively more per cent of the world’s total land and less per cent of the world’s total population. Therefore, Brazil’s population density is very less.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 20: Answer in Detail / Explain
notes.content:
(29) Giving    examples,    correlate     climate   and   population distribution.

Ans. (1) Climate and population distribution are closely related. The sparse distribution of population is found in the regions having heavy or scarce rainfall or too high or too low temperature.

(2) For example, in India, the sparse distribution of population is found in snow covered regions in Himalayan range as well as hot Thar desert. Similarly, in Brazil, the sparse distribution of population is found in the Amazon river basin receiving heavy rainfall.

(3) The dense distribution of population is found in the regions having average amount of rainfall and moderate temperature.

(4) For example, in India, the dense distribution of population is found in Ganga plains having average amount of rainfall and moderate temperature. Similarly, in Brazil, the dense distribution of population is found near southeastern coastal areas having average amount of rainfall and moderate temperature.

(30) Write a note on population growth rate in India and Brazil.

Ans. (A) Population     growth     rate    in   India : (1) In   India, population growth rate was between 2 per cent to 2.3 per cent till 1971.

(2) From 1971 to 1991, the growth rate of population in India stabilised with 2.3 per cent.

(3) From 1991, the growth rate of population in India is slowly declining.

(4) In 2011, the growth rate of population in India was 1.7 per cent.

(5) Due to steeply falling death rate and slowly falling birth rate, the population of India is still growing.

(B) Population growth rate in Brazil : (1) From 1970 to 2010, the growth rate of population in Brazil had reduced considerably.

(2) In 1970, the growth rate of population in Brazil was 3 per cent. On the contrary, in 2010, the growth rate of population in Brazil is only 0.3 per cent.

(3) Extremely limited population growth rate of Brazil indicates that population of Brazil may not increase considerably in the next two decades.

(31) Correlate climate of southeastern coastal region of Brazil and population distribution.

Ans. (1) Temperate type of climate is found in the southeastern coastal region of Brazil.

(2) Mild and humid climate, average amount of rainfall, fertile soil and availability of resources have helped in flourishing agriculture and industries in the southeastern coastal region of Brazil.

(3) These favourable factors have led to dense distribution of population in the southeastern coastal regions of Brazil.

(4) According to Census 2010, the density of population in the southeastern coastal region (in the states of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro) was the maximum, i.e. more than 300 persons per sq. km.

(32) Correlate life expectancy and social development.

Ans. (1) Increase in life expectancy indicates increase in social development of a country.

(2) Availability of medical facilities, advancement in medical sciences, availability of nutritious food, etc. factors help in increasing life expectancy.

(3) Compared to developed countries, life expectancy in developing countries is very less. Due to progress in the social and economic development in developing countries, the life expectancy in developing countries is gradually increasing.

(4) In India, in 1960, the life expectancy was only 41 years. On the contrary, in 2016 it was 68 years. This increase in life expectancy indicates increase in social development in India.

quiz.question: With reference to area, India stands at which rank in the world?
quiz.explanation: India is the seventh-largest country in the world by area.

quiz.question: Population-wise, India is the ______ largest country in the world.
quiz.explanation: India has the second-largest population in the world after China.

quiz.question: Which of the following is a favourable factor affecting population distribution?
quiz.explanation: Cultivable land provides opportunities for agriculture, which is a primary occupation and supports dense populations.

quiz.question: On the distribution of population, which factor affects it?
quiz.explanation: Physiography, or physical geography, including plains, mountains, and climate, is a major factor affecting where people settle.
